text: Interactive Grad-CAM viewer (T096): the operator drives it, an agent reads its log.

.venv/bin/python scripts/cam_viewer.py serve # http://127.0.0.1:8765 .venv/bin/python scripts/cam_viewer.py snap --study UID --label ACL .venv/bin/python scripts/cam_viewer.py notes # what was looked at and flagged .venv/bin/python scripts/cam_viewer.py selftest # maps == gradcam.py's, on real data .venv/bin/python scripts/cam_viewer.py stop # stop a detached server
WHAT IT SHOWS.
For one checkpoint (and optionally a second, for comparison), one study and one label: every slot of the bag with the label's attention weight and a Grad-CAM overlay.
The CAM is scripts/gradcam.py's, and the numbers match (selftest;
pinned in the smoke suite).
T074 showed it tracks the trained weights, not the input statistics.
The two normalisations are gradcam.py's two readings:
slice: each slice scaled to its own peak -- WHERE the evidence sits, given this slice is looked at at all;
bag: every slice on one scale for the label -- WHAT drove the logit, with attention and localisation multiplied together.
WHAT IT IS NOT.
An instrument, never a result.
Per-study pictures cannot support a column-level claim, and a defect screen can find something wrong but never confirm something right (gradcam.py's docstring;
A checkpoint trained with --train-gold has seen the gold labels, so its gold p is in-sample, and the page says so.
HOW AN AGENT MONITORS IT.

Everything lands in outputs/cam_viewer/: views.jsonl one line per (checkpoint, study, label) the operator opened, with p, gold, target and the diffuseness statistics notes.jsonl the operator's notes and flags, tied to a study, label and slot snapshots/ a PNG panel plus a JSON of its numbers;
snap makes the same panel from the CLI, so an agent can look without the page
HOW IT IS CHEAP.
One forward per study, then ONE batched autograd.grad gives all twelve labels' channel gradients: measured 0.17 s on CPU, against 3.6-4.4 s PER LABEL for a full backward().
The encoder is frozen and the hooked activation is re-rooted as a leaf, so the graph behind it is never kept and the backward stops at the layer Grad-CAM needs.
WHY CPU BY DEFAULT.
A CUDA context held by an idle viewer makes gpu_queue.sh read the card as busy, and a queued fold then defers indefinitely.
--device cuda exists;
use it only with no fold queued.
COATNET CHECKPOINTS (T113).

A coat_.pt from coat_train.py opens in a CoatEngine: the slots are the trainer's 24 evaluation windows (three slices as RGB), labelled by centre slice and by which of the corpus's five series it sits in;
the hooked layer is backbone.stages.3 (12x12 at 384).
selftest --ckpt on one runs the same two anchors.
WHY LOCAL ONLY.
The server binds 127.0.0.1.
A checkpoint is loaded only if it is in the server's own list: torch.load of an arbitrary pickle path is code execution.

noqa: E402
The wall clock on this machine is wrong (AGENTS.md).
It is used for ordering a log, never for dating a result.
What the page draws.
Operator's ruling, 2026-09-15: one method, from the library.
name -> pytorch-grad-cam class.
ONE of them is drawn;
the other is the anchor.
Imported lazily so the viewer still starts without the package.
LayerCAM is what the page shows. At the layer we hook, global average pooling follows, so every channel's gradient is constant across space.
Grad-CAM then sums w_c A_c over channels and lets a channel that pushes the logit DOWN cancel one that pushes it up;
LayerCAM keeps only the positive contributions.
Measured on armC_fold0 and one gold study's ACL, that moved edge_mass from 0.370 -- a flat map's 0.36, i.e. no localisation at all -- to 0.161.

GradCAM stays wired as the anchor, not as a choice. It is the one method the library and gradcam.py both implement, so selftest and the smoke suite compare them (8.0e-06 apart, with bit-identical activations, gradients and raw maps).
That equality is what says the library is reading OUR model correctly before LayerCAM's output is believed.
The other seven the library offers are not wired, and the measurements are in T097: HiResCAM and XGradCAM reduce to Grad-CAM here (correlation +1.000, same constant-gradient argument);
EigenCAM ignores the label;
the Eigen methods' sign is arbitrary;
RandomCAM is a weaker version of T074's control;
ScoreCAM and AblationCAM cost one masked forward per channel, which is 1,408 forwards of a 36-slice bag per label on CPU.
One line under the page's title, so what is on screen is never in doubt.
The library calls model(input_tensor) on a 4-D tensor and reads its width and height off the last two axes.
A 5-D tensor would be taken for a 3-D volume.
So the bag's slots stand in as the batch (S, 3, H, W), and mask and meta are bound here.
All labels' Grad-CAM maps from ONE vector-Jacobian call.
logits (L,) depends on act (S, C, h, w).
Row j of the identity as the grad output gives d logit_j / d act, which is exactly what gradcam.CAM gets from logits[j].backward();
the channel weights, sum and ReLU are the same.
Returns (L, S, h, w).
token-shaped activations are not supported here;
use scripts/gradcam.py for that backbone
The per-(study, label) numbers written beside every view.
attn_entropy, cam_entropy, top1_attn, top5_mass are gradcam.py's, with the same definitions, so a view and a --records row agree.
edge_mass is new: the attention-weighted share of each slice's CAM mass in the outer ring of the native grid.
edge_uniform is what a flat map would give.

Frozen, so nothing before the hooked layer keeps a graph: the hook re-roots its output as a leaf and the backward stops there.
WHICH layer, and why it is now a choice.
pick_layer(model) takes the LAST spatial module -- bn2.act for the efficientnets -- which on a 320 px frame is a 10x10 map: 32 px, and at the census's 0.5 mm per delivered pixel, 16 mm per CAM cell.
Four of the twelve findings are compartment judgements and a meniscal tear is smaller than one cell, so the default map cannot localise the thing it is being asked about.
Shallower layers are available at 8, 4, 2 and 1 mm per cell.
This is only sound because the page draws LAYERCAM.
Grad-CAM weights a channel by its gradient AVERAGED over space, which is why it degrades at shallow layers;
at bn2.act global average pooling makes that gradient constant across space anyway, so LayerCAM there reduces to Grad-CAM's positive part (T097 measured it).

Earlier in the network there are convolutions after the hook, the gradient stops being spatially constant, and LayerCAM's per-location weighting is doing real work -- which is the regime its paper was written for.

Fail when a live document cites a repository path that does not exist.
WHY THIS EXISTS.
Three tasks in a row were rejected for the same defect, and each time the stale text was in a file the same commit had edited:
T084, finding D-1 -- AGENTS.md said 975 checks, the machine said 984.
T085, findings B-2/B-3/B-5 -- six citations pointing at files those very commits had just moved, in two repo_guard entry files.
Both were found by a reviewer reading carefully, which does not scale and did not prevent the second one.
This is the same check, mechanised: a path in backticks either resolves or it does not.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN ERROR, and why each exclusion is here rather than implied.
Every one of these was a false positive in the first pass:
Dated records. PROGRESS.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/archive/, docs/research/<date>/, deaddrop/tasks/done/ and the checkpoint trails record what was true when they were written.
A citation to a file that has since moved is a correct record, not a stale claim.
T076 refused to tidy history under cover of a formatting fix;
so does this.
Generated trees. outputs/ and data/ hold artifacts that are ignored or rebuilt.
A citation to a checkpoint that no longer exists is a record of a run, and flagging it would train people to ignore this tool.
Patterns, not paths. scripts/tNNN/, tests/smoke/part_NN.py, anything containing , <, > or {, and anything ending in /.
Symbol references. tests/smoke/_order.ORDER is a module attribute written in path style.
Matched by a trailing .CapitalisedOrDotted segment that is not a known file extension.
This file. Its own docstring cites paths as examples.
An instrument that counts itself is the defect this repo keeps finding.
Markdown link labels. In [docs/RESULTS-0902](../docs/research/syntheses/RESULTS-0902-what-the-day-established.md) the backticked text is a LABEL;
the link target is what has to resolve, and it does.
Flagging the label is flagging a shortening convention.
Prose about a path's absence. A board row reading "T070 deleted scripts/t066/build_c1_kernel.py" is correct precisely BECAUSE the file is gone, and so is "never touches scripts/t075".
No static pass can read that intent, so lines carrying <!-- claims-guard-ok --> are skipped.
Every linter needs an escape hatch;
one that requires writing the reason next to the suppression is the honest shape.
HONESTY ABOUT PRECISION.
The first version of this check reported 32 hits and T086 was claimed on that number.
Reading them showed most were exclusions 6 and 7 rather than errors -- the same over-count-against-the-wrong-population defect this task exists to catch, committed by the task itself.
The raw match count is NOT a defect count;
run the guard to see what survives the exclusions.
The review also found that checking backticked paths alone repaired a link's LABEL while leaving its target dead.
Link targets are therefore checked too, and is_link_label -- which existed to guess whether a label mattered -- is gone: the target is what matters.
POPULATION.
The denominator below is path citations in backticks, in tracked markdown that is not a dated record -- not "all paths", not "all files".
The count is a floor: a path written without backticks, or built at runtime, is invisible to a static pass.
.venv/bin/python scripts/claims_guard.py # fail on any stale citation .venv/bin/python scripts/claims_guard.py --list # show them all, exit 0
Citations this repository has accepted, each with its reason.
The guard is green with these and fails on anything NEW -- a lint that is red on the day it lands gets disabled within a week.
Retire a line by fixing the citation and deleting it;
the guard reports a baseline line that is no longer stale.
Trees whose contents are tracked, so a missing citation is a real error.
outputs/ and data/ are excluded by design -- see exclusion 2.
Records of what was true when written -- exclusion 1.
outputs/ too: a report written inside a run's output directory records that run, and its citations age with it.
T093 moved the LB ledger out of outputs/, where it was a record by prefix;
it is append-only by nature and stays one.
PROJECT-LOG.md moved beside it but was LIVE at docs/ top level, and stays live.
LIVE documents that happen to sit under a record prefix.

T093 (2026-09-14) moved the cross-lane syntheses from docs/ top level -- where this guard checked them -- into docs/research/syntheses/, which the prefix above would have silently exempted: the scan dropped from 88 live files to 79, exactly the nine moved, while docs/INDEX.md still presents several as current.
A move must not change what the gate verifies, so they stay live.
A trailing segment that is not a file extension -- exclusion 4.
tests/smoke/_order.ORDER is an attribute, not a file.

Added after T086's review.
A backticked path has no declared intent, which is why checking one needs seven exclusions and why two of this task's own "fixes" repaired a label and left its target dead.
A LINK target has intent: it either resolves from the document that contains it, or the hyperlink is broken.
repo_guard.py already does this correctly for four entry documents;
this is the same resolution widened to every live one.
(file, line, citation) for every live citation that does not resolve.
A backticked path that is a LINK LABEL is display text;
the target is the checkable claim and broken_links() checks it directly.
This is not the old is_link_label guess, which asked whether the target resolved and so let a broken link through whenever its label happened to be valid.
A document may DECLARE a numeric claim, and the guard verifies it exactly:
<!-- claim: lines scripts/smoke_test.py 135 --> <!-- claim: func-lines src/train.py run 622 -->
Declared rather than inferred, and that is the whole point.

T086 and T087 both began by scanning prose for numbers, and both produced garbage: a scanner cannot tell a function's length from its file's, a historical figure from a live one, or which of three numbers on a line belongs to which of two paths.
A declaration names its referent, so it has no false positives by construction and needs no exclusion list at all.
Any line that LOOKS like a declaration.
A typo in a marker used to be silently skipped, which removes the protection it was written to provide and tells nobody -- a lint that fails open (T087 review, M-1).
A marker inside a fence or inline backticks is an ILLUSTRATION, not an assertion.
Without this the syntax cannot be documented without asserting it, and the guard eventually fires on a dated record whose only route back to green is editing the record (M-2).
(file, line, description) for every DECLARED claim that is now false.
Strip inline-code spans first: a marker shown inside backticks is documentation of the syntax, not an assertion.

Without this the syntax cannot be written down anywhere without being checked, and the guard eventually fires on a dated record whose only route back to green is editing the record (T087 review, M-2).

Module level first: a declaration about run means the top-level run, not a helper nested inside another function. src/train.py has two, and the shipped claim resolved correctly only because ast.walk happens to be breadth-first -- luck, not design (M-3).
"a declaration names its referent" is FALSE for a non-unique name. src/model.py has four forwards and src/train.py has two runs;
the shipped claim resolved correctly only because ast.walk is breadth-first, which is luck rather than design (M-3).
docs/CAPABILITIES.md states a flag count;
the parser is the truth.

That file exists to watch the gap between what the CLI accepts and what runs pass, and T086 found it had gone stale for nine days -- off by one even on the day it was written -- while AGENTS.md cited it twice as authoritative.
A watcher nobody watches is the defect it was built to prevent.
Assert the SET too.
T086's first pass asserted only the count and got the SET wrong, in the direction of calling a never-passed flag passed, because it matched a smoke-check NAME echoed into a log.
The count would not have caught that;
nothing would have.
FOLLOW SYMLINKS.

Path.rglob does not, and on 2026-09-20 that turned a disk cleanup into a false alarm: / hit 98%, eight closed task trees under outputs/ were archived to another drive and symlinked back, and this guard -- which proves a claim ABOUT THE PROJECT'S HISTORY -- stopped seeing the logs that record which flags were passed.
It reported 11 never-passed flags against a page saying four, from evidence that had not changed at all.
A guard whose answer depends on which directories happen to be symlinks is measuring the filesystem, not the claim.
os.walk(followlinks=True) reads through them;
seen keeps a link that points back inside the tree from being walked twice. ...AND FOLLOWING A SYMLINK TO A DRIVE THAT IS NOT THERE FINDS NOTHING EITHER.

Measured 2026-09-21, hours after the fix above: the disk holding the archive is USB, it dropped off the bus mid-session (device 8:1 no longer exists, twice in six minutes), and all eight links went dangling.

os.walk(followlinks=True) then walks into nothing and this guard prints the IDENTICAL false alarm the paragraph above was written to end -- "says four, finds 11" -- from evidence that, once again, had not changed.
So the fix above was necessary and not sufficient: it repaired HOW the tree is read and not WHETHER the tree is there.
A guard that proves a claim about the project's history must REFUSE when its evidence is unreachable, never quietly compute a number from the part that survived.

Failing for the wrong reason is the same defect class as passing for the wrong reason, and it costs more here, because this one fails make check -- the command this repository tells every contributor to run before pushing to Kaggle -- and names the wrong culprit while doing it.

REFUSING to count never-passed flags: the evidence is unreachable.n {len(dangling)} dangling symlink(s) under outputs/: {', '.join(dangling)}nThese point at an archive on an external disk that is not mounted.

The logsnrecording which flags were passed live behind them, so any count taken nowndescribes the filesystem and not the project's history -- it would reportn~11 never-passed flags against a page that correctly says four.nRemount the archive, or restore the trees, before trusting this guard.

It was parsed in two places, which is how the LINK prefix came to be treated as a path entry in one of them and reported every link as a settled debt -- a bookkeeping bug in the guard's own bookkeeping.
A baseline entry that is no longer stale is itself an error: the debt was paid and the record was not updated, which is this task's whole subject.
Does the morning's gold-58 predict what the kernel will actually do?

Registered in deaddrop/tasks/T112-the-4090-first-day.md BEFORE this ran, after review found the gap: the trainer reaches the model's 224 px from the 336 corpus in one bilinear step, while the kernel decodes the DICOM to 384 and then resizes to 224 -- 1.714x non-antialiased decimation against 1.5x.
It also evaluates with the native384-v8 group's k_eval 42, where the trainer scored gold-58 with 24 windows.
Three conditions, same checkpoint, same 58 studies, same device and precision:

A 336 -> 224, k 24 what the trainer measured (0.8848 on GPU/bf16) C 336 -> 224, k 42 the kernel's window count, the trainer's resample B 336 -> 384 -> 224, k 42 the kernel's window count AND its resample chain
So C - A isolates the window count and B - C the resample chain.
The registered rule: if |B - A| >= 0.036 -- the gold-58 noise band -- the morning's reading does not predict the kernel and must NOT be used to clear the BROKEN floor for this submission.
What B approximates, stated plainly: the kernel's 384 volume is a direct INTER_AREA decode of the DICOM;
here it is the 336 corpus upsampled to 384 and then downsampled.
That adds an upsampling step the kernel does not have, so B is an approximation of the chain, not a replica of it.
The DICOM path would need the kernel's own decode, which is outside what a 58-study check should build.
Runs on CPU by default: it is meant for the cooldown gap after a fold, and a CUDA context would restart any queued fold's 20-minute gate (T067).

Where the adopted CoAtNet arm looks: Grad-CAM for a coat_train.py checkpoint.
scripts/gradcam.py is the instrument for the superseded b2 KneeMIL.
It rebuilds the model from the args a train.py checkpoint stores, which a coat_train.py checkpoint does not carry -- it stores recipe -- so it cannot open one.
This is the same instrument for CoatMIL.

It writes gradcam.py's cells.csv schema and run.json, so scripts/cam_sheet.py builds the contact sheet unchanged, and it imports the helpers that carry the method (upsample, per-window normalisation, entropy, ranking, thumbnails) rather than copying them.
Where the graph starts. The encoder is frozen and runs with no graph;
the map Grad-CAM is taken on is then made a leaf that requires grad, and only what sits above it -- the timm head, and for --layer stages.2 stage 3 as well -- runs on a graph.
The gradient reaching that leaf is exactly the one gradcam.CAM captures with a hook, since nothing between the map and the logit is skipped;
what is saved is the encoder's activations, which is what lets 24 windows at 384 fit the laptop's 8 GiB card with room to spare.
A window, not a slice. A study is a bag of k_eval windows, each three consecutive slices stacked as RGB (coat_data.py).
Panels draw the centre slice of each window and name the window by that slice's index.
The windows are the trainer's own deterministic evaluation windows, so the pictures show the bag the recorded gold score was measured on.
Three gates, pre-registered in T113, before any picture is believed:
G1 the split forward reproduces CoatMIL.forward (checked on the first study of every run);
G2 over all gold studies, the AUC and per-study probabilities reproduce the checkpoint's own saved evaluation (<stem>.gold_pred.npz);
G3 the map equals pytorch-grad-cam's GradCAM on the same layer (--g3;
it needs a full graph through the encoder, so it runs at reduced k).
Two defect screens ride along per cell, both attention-weighted over windows: frame_share (CAM mass on the outermost ring of the native grid;
uniform is 0.306 at 12x12) and air_ratio (CAM mass density on near-black pixels relative to their area;
1.0 is indifferent).
T113 holds their thresholds.
What this is not. An instrument, not a lever: see gradcam.py's docstring.
Per-study pictures cannot carry a column-level claim on n=58.

T100's BatchNorm recalibration driver: the estimator and the guards.

The driver rewrites ONLY BatchNorm buffers, and it computes them itself rather than letting PyTorch average per batch, because valid-slice counts per study are not equal and a batch-average would weight a small batch like a large one.

These checks pin the arithmetic, the fingerprint that refuses a learned-tensor change, and the two shapes that make the pass safe: gathered encoding must equal dense encoding, and an all-padding bag must never reach the encoder.
-- the estimator: pooled mean and Bessel-corrected variance over everything the BN saw, independent of how it was chopped into batches.
A batch-average would differ here, which is the whole reason for the hook.
-- the fingerprint ignores BN buffers and catches a learned tensor.
-- gather == dense in eval mode, and an all-padding bag yields nothing.

Kill a training run that has provably stopped making progress.

WHY THIS EXISTS: twice now a fold has hung mid-run with the main thread spinning in userspace, the GPU at 0%, and zero disk I/O -- T004 at epoch 8 (killed after 62 min) and T007 at epoch 6 (killed after 1 h 43 m).
Both were noticed by a human looking at /proc.

A hang now costs ~20 minutes of card time instead of an unattended night, and the job script's own recovery runs afterwards instead of not at all.
THE STALL TEST IS AN AND, deliberately:
the log has not grown AND nvidia-smi utilization is 0%
for STALL_MIN consecutive minutes.
Either signal alone is a false positive.
The log does not grow during a normal 30-minute training epoch, because train.py prints once per epoch -- so log-silence alone would kill every run.
And utilization dips to 0% between batches, so a single 0% sample means nothing.
Only both together, held for twenty minutes, describe the observed hang: no kernels launched, no batches consumed, nothing written.
BEFORE KILLING IT ASKS FOR A STACK.

train.py's arm_diagnostics() registers faulthandler on SIGUSR1, whose handler runs at the C level without the GIL, so it dumps every thread's Python frames even while the main thread is spinning inside a C call.
Neither previous hang could be read (ptrace_scope=1, no sudo, so no py-spy);
the next one will be, in the trainer's own log.
OCCUPANCY COMES FROM nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps, NEVER FROM A PGREP PATTERN.
A watcher whose command line contains the pattern it waits for matches itself;
that is how five shells once deadlocked here (CLAUDE.md, PROGRESS.md).
